items.issue: Weak or slow hook — first 3 seconds have low energy, small text, and no clear value proposition. Framing is wide so the subject is hard to read on small screens; audio level dips and there's no distinct sound cue.
items.suggestion: Recut/re-shoot the opening so the value is explicit in 0–2s: use a tight close‑up, big readable caption (large sans‑serif, high contrast), and a loud audio cue or voice‑over stating the benefit. Start on an action or surprising visual, add a 0.25s sound punch on frame 1, and cut to a 1–2s visual that proves the hook. Keep motion simple (push in / quick jump cut) to maximize retention on mobile.

educationalResources.topic: How to Hook Viewers Quickly (InVideo guide)

nextSteps: Reshoot 0–5s: film a close‑up with the on‑screen benefit spoken in one sentence, add a 0.25s audio punch at 0s, and display a single large caption that matches the spoken hook.
Create two variant opens (A/B): Variant A = bold visual + voice hook; Variant B = question + text overlay. Upload both and compare retention after 24–48 hours.
Add subtitles (editable text overlay) and a high‑contrast thumbnail frame pulled from the 0–3s mark.
Watch the three linked resources and implement one lighting/frame adjustment and one sound cue change before the next upload.
